record.context_brief: Hyperbolic actions generated by finite-order elements
record.original_question: In Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension, does there exist a discrete cocompact isometric action generated entirely by elements of finite order?

evidence.quote: Consider the Lobachevsky space of sufficiently large dimension. Does it admit a discrete cocompact isometric action generated by (a) elements of finite order?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{H}^n$ denote the $n$-dimensional Lobachevsky (real hyperbolic) space, and let $\operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ be its full isometry group. A subgroup $\Gamma \leq \operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ is said to act discretely and cocompactly if $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup and the quotient $\mathbb{H}^n / \Gamma$ is compact. An element $g \in \operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ is said to be of finite order if $g^k = \mathrm{id}$ for some positive integer $k$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n_0$ such that for all $n \geq n_0$ (or, more weakly, for some sufficiently large $n$) there is a discrete cocompact subgroup $\Gamma \leq \operatorname{Isom}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ which is generated, as an abstract group, entirely by elements of finite order?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether, in sufficiently high-dimensional hyperbolic space, there exists a discrete cocompact isometry group generated by finite-order elements appears to be an open problem. Cocompact arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups (which are generated by involutions) are known to exist only in bounded dimension (no compact hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes exist in $\mathbb{H}^n$ for $n \geq 30$, with examples of Bugaenko in moderate dimensions), and the broader question of generation by torsion elements in high dimension is expected to have a negative answer but is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Arithmetic hyperbolic reflection groups (Belolipetsky)
status_evidence.snippet: There are no compact hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes and no arithmetic finite volume Coxeter polytopes in H^n for n>29; cocompact examples in higher dimensions due to Bugaenko require quadratic forms over fields of degree ≥2.
status_evidence.claim: Cocompact hyperbolic reflection groups (generated by involutions) exist only in bounded dimension, suggesting torsion-generated cocompact lattices are constrained.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Coxeter groups of large dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions and limits on hyperbolic Coxeter groups in large dimension.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the dimensional bounds for groups generated by reflections (finite-order elements) acting cocompactly on hyperbolic space.
